title: Spread of the Arabic language
summary: Classical Arabic, the language of the Quran, began to spread during the Islamic expansion of the 7th and 8th centuries. It replaced Aramaic in the Levant, along with other languages. In Iran it became the language of the dominant class, of religion and government, and by extension of science and literature. Today more than 100 million people are native speakers, by one older estimate.

uncertainty.note: Arabic expanded outward from the 630s CE with the early Islamic conquests, becoming the administrative standard under Abd al-Malik c. 700 CE and cementing its vernacular dominance by the 10th–11th centuries.

as_recorded.value: Islamic expansion of the 7th and 8th centuries

where.modern_name: Middle East and North Africa; stand-in pin at Damascus, Syria
where.historical_name: Dimashq, capital of the Umayyad Caliphate

importance.justification: Created a unified linguistic and literary realm across the Middle East and North Africa, reshaping regional vernaculars and creating a global scholarly language.

related.because: Military expansion established Arab rule across the Levant, Egypt, North Africa, and Persia, enabling administrative Arabization.
